briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and Google Gemini 3 push frontier capabilities amid escalating compute race

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs released multiple high-capability models in the past week, driving record funding and infrastructure commitments. Regulatory scrutiny intensifies as governments race to classify advanced systems. Prompt injection and multi-agent security remain top operational risks across deployments.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed o4 with native tool-use and long-horizon planning. Anthropic released Claude 4 Opus while Google launched Gemini 3 with 2M context. Meta open-sourced Llama 4 405B variant and DeepSeek published R2 reasoning model.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidance on agentic systems released; several red-team reports highlight persistent jailbreak success rates above 40%.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: Microsoft announced $15B Texas supercluster expansion. TSMC began volume production of 2nm AI chips for Nvidia and Broadcom. xAI secured 200k H100-equivalent GPUs for Memphis cluster.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first model to demonstrate sustained autonomous R&D emerge before 2028?
